methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 6 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waymo is a late-stage private company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, currently valued at $126B following $16B+ in cumulative capital raised. The relevant peer universe consists of 6 private companies in the same sector, including Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation. No public comparables exist in this narrow category.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable here. While 6 same-sector peers exist, none meet narrow filtering criteria—specifically, no peers fall into the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. This absence of sufficiently tight comparables (a threshold of ≥3 datapoints was required) renders a median-based approach unreliable and potentially misleading. Falling back to an all-sector median would introduce excessive heterogeneity and obscure stage and scale differences material to pricing.

The current $126B valuation cannot be independently triangulated using standard VC methodology against peer data. This reflects both Waymo's scale—at the upper end of private company valuations—and the nascent, dispersed nature of the autonomous vehicle and drone ecosystem, where few peers have reached comparable funding or capitalization milestones. Resolution of valuation uncertainty would require either: (1) materialization of public comparables with meaningful scale, or (2) transaction evidence from the existing peer set. Investors should treat this valuation as primarily driven by prior round pricing power and strategic positioning rather than derived from comparable-company analysis.
